vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP vulnerability in a transport-only sibling artifact.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll provides Linux epoll(7) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. The cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* CPE causes OWASP to propagate the CVE here. Liquibase does not expose any HTTP server; the vulnerable chunked-encoding decoder is unreachable from this artifact regardless.

vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP/2 server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP/2 vulnerability in a transport-only sibling artifact.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll is the Linux epoll native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE here despite the artifact not containing the vulnerable parser.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty's epoll transport fails to detect and close TCP connections that receive a RST after being half-closed, leading to stale channels that are never cleaned up and, in some code paths, a 100% CPU busy-loop in the event loop thread.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a Netty server.

ratings.justification: Liquibase never accepts inbound connections on any Netty transport, including epoll; Netty is only used as a client transport for outbound database driver connections.

analysis.detail: Netty 4.2.x splits the epoll native transport into two Maven coordinates: netty-transport-classes-epoll (the Java-side channel/ event-loop implementation, including EpollSocketChannel) and netty-transport-native-epoll (the per-platform JNI bindings). Both ship as part of the same logical epoll transport as the sibling netty-transport-native-epoll assessment above, and the same reachability argument applies directly here — not as a scanner over-match like the netty-transport entry above, since this artifact genuinely contains the affected EpollSocketChannel RST-handling code. Confirmed present at the vulnerable version 4.2.9.Final on the published liquibase-secure:5.2.0 image (scan-results branch commit 8c9d0ffdf1, 2026-07-31 run, liquibase/liquibase-secure/5.2.0/trivy-deep.json), within the affected 4.2.0.Final-4.2.13.Final range. A repo-wide grep for Netty server bootstrap usage (`grep -rln "ServerBootstrap" --include="*.java" .`) returns zero hits: Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that never runs a network server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver, used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections, so there is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.
